# The Epoch Institute

> A historical research site: 490 full profiles of empires, states, religions, languages, cultures and movements, a 32,149-entry encyclopedia, a register of
> 5,468 states and their 11,296 connections, country histories, century overviews, an interactive world atlas
> (3500 BCE to today), and the data behind them, free to download.

All reference pages are static HTML with the content in the page itself. Dates use CE/BCE. British English. Profiles,
century pages and reading paths end with "Test yourself": a few questions built only from that page's own data.

## Collections
- [Profiles](https://the-epoch-institute.org/profiles): the 426 in-depth profiles of empires and states, from Rome and the Mughals to Tonga, Cahokia and Great Zimbabwe (history, power curve, key facts, references) at /empire/<slug>
- [Religions](https://the-epoch-institute.org/profiles?kind=religion): 18 profiles of faiths, from Hinduism and Judaism to Norse religion and the Bahá'í Faith, at /religion/<slug> (origins, beliefs, texts, spread, community, legacy)
- [Languages](https://the-epoch-institute.org/profiles?kind=language): 16 profiles of languages, from Sumerian and Latin to Nahuatl and Swahili, at /language/<slug> (origins, structure, speakers, literature, change, legacy)
- [Cultures](https://the-epoch-institute.org/profiles?kind=culture): 15 profiles of cultures and civilisations, from the Indus Valley, the Minoans and the Olmecs to the Lapita, the Vikings and the Ancestral Puebloans, at /culture/<slug> (origins, society, beliefs, arts, exchange, legacy)
- [Movements](https://the-epoch-institute.org/profiles?kind=movement): 15 profiles of movements, from Renaissance humanism and the Reformation to the Bhakti saints, the Nahda and the civil rights and anti-apartheid movements, at /movement/<slug> (background, aims, events, people, outcomes, legacy)
- [Encyclopedia](https://the-epoch-institute.org/encyclopedia/): people, events, places, ideas and works; one page per entry at /encyclopedia/<slug>
- [States register](https://the-epoch-institute.org/state/): every recorded state at /state/<id>, with origins, rule and legacy
- [Country histories](https://the-epoch-institute.org/countries/): the states that ruled each present-day country
- [Centuries](https://the-epoch-institute.org/centuries/): one page per century, 30th century BCE to the 21st
- [Year by year](https://the-epoch-institute.org/years/): what happened in a single year, at /years/<year> (/years/1453, /years/480-bce)
- [People](https://the-epoch-institute.org/people/): the encyclopedia's 12,992 people by century and region, at /people/<century>
- [Today in history](https://the-epoch-institute.org/today-in-history/): a page for each day of the year, with at least eight events and the people born and died that day (dates as the sources give them, Julian before 1582)
- [Great speeches](https://the-epoch-institute.org/speeches/): 80 speeches from Xerxes to Reagan, with the setting, a key passage and, where free, the full text
- [Reading paths](https://the-epoch-institute.org/paths/): 38 guided routes through the profiles and the encyclopedia
- [Research Series](https://the-epoch-institute.org/research-series): five essays at /essays/<slug> on power, trade, collapse, cultural exchange and military change, each ending with what the Institute's data shows
- [Glossary](https://the-epoch-institute.org/encyclopedia/glossary): 723 historical terms
- [Community](https://the-epoch-institute.org/community): readers' opinions and articles (at /articles/<slug>: the authors' own views and sources, not checked by the Institute), each read by the Institute before it appears

## Tools
- [Search](https://the-epoch-institute.org/search): every profile, state and entry, filtered by kind, region and century (/search?q=<words>)
- [Atlas](https://the-epoch-institute.org/atlas): the world's states in any year, on a globe or a flat map; "What was here?" lists the states whose seat lay within 250 km of any place (or the reader's own location, which stays in the browser), oldest first
- [World timeline](https://the-epoch-institute.org/timeline): every state on one timeline, region by region
- [Connections](https://the-epoch-institute.org/connections): how states were linked — rule, vassalage, lineage
- [Empire Explorer](https://the-epoch-institute.org/explorer): power trajectories compared
- [Rise and Fall Race](https://the-epoch-institute.org/race): up to four states and empires race year by year, each power curve weighted by the state's scores in the Institute's analysis; presets (the steppe empires, the caliphates, the Andes, West Africa …), shareable addresses (?p=slugs&y=year)
- [Write in Ancient Scripts](https://the-epoch-institute.org/write): a keyboard for twelve languages of the past in their own scripts (cuneiform, hieroglyphs, Linear B, runes, Brahmi, Orkhon …), each sign with its value and sound; also on each language's profile
- [History Games](https://the-epoch-institute.org/games): eleven games, among them a daily History Connections, History Crossword and Who Said It? (five quotations a day, each word for word from a public-domain edition or translation, named under the answer), Order the Ranks (a society's ranks to put in order), Word Hunt in sixteen themes and Picture Puzzle in six sets
- [Social Ladders](https://the-epoch-institute.org/societies/): the social hierarchies of societies from Old Babylonia to the Russian Empire, each from the ruler down to the enslaved: every rank with its share of the population (from named scholarly estimates, or "no reliable count"), its rights and duties, and how people rose or fell; a pyramid drawn by rank or to scale, two societies compared rank by rank, and "Born into history", a life drawn at random by the ranks' shares
- [Flashcards](https://the-epoch-institute.org/flashcards): decks made from the collections (the glossary's terms, the people of each century, the capitals and dated key events of the profiles by region, the stops of each reading path), learned with spaced repetition in the reader's browser
- [Faith Maps](https://the-epoch-institute.org/faiths): eighteen religions on a turning globe (or a flat map) century by century — where each began, how it spread, where it was a main faith or held communities, and where it last lived on; also on each religion's profile

## Data
- [Open Data](https://the-epoch-institute.org/dataset): the states register, relations and power curves as CSV and JSON
- [Today in history feed](https://the-epoch-institute.org/feeds/today.xml): RSS, one item a day
- [Research Series feed](https://the-epoch-institute.org/feed.xml): RSS, one item per essay
- [Sitemap](https://the-epoch-institute.org/sitemap.xml)
